steps.prompt: {{workflow_brief}}

Work directly on branch main in C:\source\parityproven (no worktree; base commit 9719595). Investigate and write an ordered plan to C:/source/parityproven/.agents/tasks/adversarial-review/plan.md. Read first: .kiro/steering/*.md (verification-standard, claims-and-evidence, sources-and-data, structure, tech, product, pair-records), README.md, .kiro/specs/step2-coverage/design.md, src/cli/agreed-tests.ts, src/agreed/generate.ts, src/conversions/specs*.ts, src/pairs/status.ts, src/cli/log-effort.ts, src/cli/review-packet.ts, src/receipts/builder.ts, web/app.js, scripts/mutate-check.ps1, .tmp/reset-step5.mjs.

TASK (verbatim): Build and run an 'adversarial review gate' for the ParityProven T-SQL -> PL/pgSQL verification harness in C:\source\parityproven (TypeScript, Node 22, ESM; npm scripts in package.json; Docker stack with SQL Server and PostgreSQL already running as docker-mssql-1 / docker-postgres-1). Commit locally with explicit paths; DO NOT push. No Co-Authored-By / 'Generated with' trailers.
OWNER DECISIONS (made, do not revisit): A1 B1 C1.
- A1: the gate is required between step 4 and step 5 for every object. Step 5 stays a HUMAN sign-off, but on the gate's evidence report instead of line-by-line code reading. Record this as a new ruling in .kiro/steering/verification-standard.md (owner, 2026-11-18, A1): step 5 = the owner's review of the adversarial evidence report against the step-5 checklist, at least one day after the first pass. Keep product.md's claim TRUE: 'no language model in the pass/fail verdict'.
- B1: two independent agents per object: an ATTACKER that writes cases designed to make the engines disagree, and an AUDITOR that checks the attacker's cases are real attacks, cover every applicable trap, and that each label matches what was sent. Use different models for attacker and auditor if more than one model is available; record the model of each in the evidence.
- C1: run the gate on all 44 objects that pass steps 1-4: the 37 pending and the 7 verified. List them from pairs/<db>/*.json (status pending or verified, or evidence step1-4 pass/n-a).
CORE RULE: agents never decide pass/fail. Every attack must become a deterministic fixed case that the harness runs on both engines (src/cli/agreed-tests.ts, src/agreed/generate.ts, spec fixedCases in src/conversions/specs*.ts). Any engine disagreement = a finding (fail). No disagreement = 'N adversarial cases ran, 0 differed', never 'agent approved'.
WHAT TO BUILD (design is the workflow's; record it in a new spec .kiro/specs/adversarial-review/{requirements,design,tasks}.md, matching the style of .kiro/specs/step2-coverage/):
1. A place for adversarial cases separate from the hand-derived ones (e.g. an ObjectSpec field or committed per-object files), clearly marked as agent-written on receipts and in tests/<db>/.
2. Running them through the existing step-2 machinery on both engines (tSQLt / plain SQL; FOR JSON procedures use the client re-run per ruling J1). Expected values captured from the ORIGINAL T-SQL only.
3. Adequacy: the adversarial cases must catch the object's planted defects (spec mutants or autoMutants), reported per object.
4. Evidence per object: evidence/adversarial/<db>/<Object>.json with attacker model, auditor model, every case (label, trap targeted, reasoning), harness result per case per engine, auditor objections, mutant adequacy, timestamps. A per-batch human-readable report in evidence/adversarial/reports/ mapping each step-5 checklist item (the 10 items in src/cli/review-packet.ts output) to evidence.
5. Receipts (src/receipts/builder.ts, web/app.js) show the adversarial result. Status rule stays in src/pairs/status.ts only; the gate must be passed before step 5 can be recorded.
6. An owner approval CLI (e.g. npm run approve -- --report <path> --reviewer "<name>" --date <yyyy-mm-dd>) that records step 5 for the objects in a report, refusing any object with a divergence, an unresolved auditor objection, or inadequate attacks; it enforces the one-day rule like src/cli/log-effort.ts. Agents and workflow steps must NEVER run it or otherwise record step 5.
7. Unit tests for the new code (vitest, src/**/*.test.ts), with planted defects checked like scripts/mutate-check.ps1.
FINDINGS: if an attack makes the engines disagree, follow .kiro/specs/step2-coverage/requirements.md REQ-4.3: record it, keep Kiro's previous conversion as conversions/<db>/<Object>.draft.sql if none exists, fix the conversion in the open, keep the failing case as a regression case, re-run convert (steps 1, 3, 4) and agreed-tests. If the object was verified, reset its step 5 (see .tmp/reset-step5.mjs pattern; note why on the pair record). Never weaken a case to make it pass.
CONSTRAINTS: Never run two harness processes (convert, agreed-tests, run-all) at once: they share scratch databases. Do not rebuild dist/ while one runs. The agent's pwsh shell often hangs (returns only '^C'); the command usually keeps running. Use one command per call, redirect output to a NEW log file, check state before retrying; start long jobs as background processes and poll a status file. README status block is generated (npm run readme:status / receipts:build); never type counts. Wording rules in claims-and-evidence.md apply.

The plan must fix: the data model for adversarial cases, the file layout, the evidence JSON schema, how a batch of objects is attacked/audited/run (attacker writes cases to a committed per-object file, auditor writes objections into the evidence, a CLI command runs them on both engines and computes mutant adequacy and writes evidence and the batch report), and the exact list of the 44 objects, split into 4 batches of 11 in order of database then object name (write the list to C:/source/parityproven/.agents/tasks/adversarial-review/batches.md). You may restructure the remaining workflow steps. If your exploration concludes this work decomposes into separable features, author the FEAT artifacts under C:/source/parityproven/.agents/tasks/adversarial-review/ and replace the remaining steps via update_workflow, per your restructuring instructions. If it does not decompose, just write the plan; the existing loop will implement it.
